rationale: All three lenses ran against the 2,174-line source diff in full; the 3,389-line test diff was reviewed only by the acceptance lens for coverage, so confidence is low per the oversized-diff rule. Four actionable gaps (CR-001..CR-004: missing log warnings, path order, reserved-path fold order, a missing copy-on-write test). Deferred (5, not emitted): stale download access after a skill is unshared, a pre-existing user file at a target path is skipped without a notice, skip notices appear only on the seeding turn, no index on blob_owner/blob_name for the D2 lookup, and the legacy notice wording is not verbatim. About 15 further concerns were dismissed after checking the code (for example the production unique constraint exists, edits are copy-on-write, the migration was unmerged).

findings.title: Skipped and inline skill files are not logged
findings.problem: The skip messages built from the plan go only to the model; the only logger.warning calls are the collision and the exception handler.
findings.impact: The story and spec require a warning to be logged for older (inline) skills and for files over the limits; operators cannot see them.
findings.recommendation: Log a warning naming the skill, the folder and the skip reasons whenever the plan skips anything.

findings.title: Over-ceiling cut is not made in path order
findings.problem: plan_bundle_seed walks the refs in stored (upload) order; nothing sorts them by path.
findings.impact: The story says files are made available in path order while they fit, so which files survive a ceiling depends on upload order.
findings.recommendation: Iterate sorted(files, key=lambda ref: ref.path) and add a test with an unsorted bundle that exceeds the count limit.

findings.title: Reserved-path fold runs after normpath
findings.problem: is_reserved_path normalizes separators with normpath first and applies NFKC/casefold afterwards, so a compatibility character that folds into a separator or dot (fullwidth slash, fullwidth backslash) is never collapsed.
findings.impact: The rule is advertised as Unicode-insensitive; a spelling that folds to a bridge path after normalization can slip past callers that use the function directly, such as the export filter.
findings.recommendation: Fold first (NFKC + casefold), then replace backslashes, then normpath and strip the leading slash; add test cases with fullwidth separators.

findings.title: No test proves a user edit leaves the skill's stored file untouched
findings.problem: The behavior (copy-on-write in _upsert_workspace_file_content) is correct, but no test seeds a skill-owned row, edits or overwrites it, and asserts the skill blob is not written and the row is repointed to a workspace-owned blob.
findings.impact: This is a stated acceptance criterion and the main isolation guarantee of the reference design; a regression would corrupt a skill for every workspace.
findings.recommendation: Add a service test: upsert/edit a row with blob_owner 'skill-sk1', assert file_repository.write_file is called with owner 'workspace-<id>' only and the row's blob_owner/blob_name are repointed.
